symptom: SQL <alias> GENERATE CONNECTOR INTO <Module> emitted queries that cannot run against the database they were generated from: `SELECT id, CustomerNumber, Name, Email, Active FROM customer` -> `ERROR: Table with name customer does not exist! Did you mean "cdcpublish.customer"?`. Worse and quieter: a table name that two schemas share was refused as ambiguous by the describe step and the object was dropped from the output entirely, so three views in gave one entity out with no warning (ako/mxcli#2414).
cause: ShowTables/ShowViews return (table_schema, table_name) and both readers kept only row[1] (sql/schema.go ReadAllTableSchemas, ReadAllViewSchemas), so TableSchema.Schema -- a field that already existed -- was never populated and the emitter had nothing to qualify with; generate.go then addressed the table as ts.Name. The drop is the second-order effect: ReadTableSchema on a bare name hits refuseAmbiguousTable, which correctly refuses a name in two schemas, and the reader's `continue // skip tables that fail` swallows it.
file: sql/schema.go (ReadAllTableSchemas, ReadAllViewSchemas, ReadTableSchema, new tableAddresses/qualifiedTableName/TableSchema.QualifiedName); sql/generate.go (renderConnector, extracted from GenerateConnector); test sql/generate_schema_qualified_2414_test.go
insight: The whole sql/ metadata pipeline runs end to end with no PostgreSQL: modernc SQLite, DriverPostgres so the real query templates execute, and `ATTACH ':memory:' AS information_schema` with tables/columns fixtures (the harness the IMPORT ... LINK fix established in sql/import_assoc_test.go). Use it -- the repo's other DB-backed sql tests are gated on MXCLI_TEST_PG_DSN and therefore skip in CI, which is how ako/mxcli#808 shipped green, and the lake this was found against is DuckDB, which rejects `serial` so it cannot host them either. Two controls, each on the end-to-end test: emitter back to ts.Name -> every FROM unqualified; reader back to row[1] -> same, plus `1 entities, want 3`. The reason the defect survived is that it is invisible on exactly the database most people try: a single schema in the connection's search path works, and in the live reproduction 1 of 6 generated queries passed for that reason (main.ro_probe). Reserved words are a red herring -- bare `FROM order` is a syntax error, but `FROM cdcpublish.order` parses, so qualifying subsumes it; whether quoting is still needed is unmeasured on strict PostgreSQL. Found by pointing mxcli at a DuckGraphLake lake serving Mendix entity CDC, where every publishing app gets a schema of its own, so nothing is in the search path.
